subject: Performance SLO — Private/VPC network qualification (Novaca)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novaca.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up — Private/VPC network qualification

Alex — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we have alignment before the technical validation: 

Summary of requirements we heard
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 150ms end-to-end for inference responses (target for initial rollout).
- Throughput: sustained 50 requests/sec across your peak hourly window; burst to 200 req/sec for short periods.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~200 active sessions, with spikes to 500.
- Streaming: partial token streaming required for responses >1s to improve UX.

Network/Private deployment items we need to validate
1) Preferred connectivity model: VPC peering vs. customer-managed VPN (you mentioned both on the call). We need your preference and any infra constraints.
2) Egress IPs/NAT: list of source IP ranges that will be allowed to reach your services and which ports will be open.
3) Latency budget inside your network: expected internal hop latencies and any firewall/proxy timeouts we should plan for.
4) Peering/BGP or VPN config details: route tables, MTU, and whether you can support jumbo frames (recommended for large payloads).
5) Test window: proposed time(s) when we can run synthetic load tests from Redwood into your VPC.

Attached: slo-checklist.pdf and network-specs.csv (lightweight templates to fill in).

Next steps
- Alex: can you share the egress IPs and preferred connectivity approach?
- NetOps: if convenient, share a network diagram and any ACLs that we should mirror for the test.
- Jordan/Ethan: once we have egress IPs, please queue load test sim and config the streaming tests.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0192

Attachment stubs: slo-checklist.pdf (template), network-specs.csv (fields: region, vpc-id, subnet-ips, mtu)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novaca.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Network Operations <netops@novaca.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — Private/VPC network qualification

Thanks Marissa, good summary. A few answers below and attached a current network diagram and our VPN config export.

Answers
- Latency: p95 target of 150ms is correct and acceptable. Our internal targets are tighter (p95 internal hops ~40ms) but we expect ~80ms additional external latency to a hosted provider.
- Throughput: sustained 50 req/s is expected; we can support bursts to 250 req/s for short windows during batch jobs.
- Concurrency: current concurrent sessions average 180 with 500 peak during end-of-month reports.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for the UI team; partial token delivery will be important.

Connectivity
- Preferred approach: AWS VPC peering where possible (we're in us-west-2). If peering isn't available, we will stand up a customer-managed IPsec VPN.
- Egress IPs: we'll provide a list from NetOps (see CC). For peering we will share route targets.
- Firewall timeouts: our edge firewalls have a 120s default TCP idle timeout; we can extend for specific flows if needed.

Attachments
- current-network-diagram.png (high level)
- vpn-config.txt (export of our IPSec config)

I'll ask NetOps to follow up with the concrete egress IP list and a copy of the ACLs. Happy to coordinate a test window next week, prefer mornings PST.

Best,
Alex Morgan
Director, Platform Engineering — Novaca Health
alex.morgan@novaca.com

Attachment stubs: current-network-diagram.png, vpn-config.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novaca.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — Private/VPC network qualification

Alex — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. Couple of quick items from our ops side so we can prep tests and configs: 

1) Egress IPs: once NetOps sends the list we'll add them to our firewall allowlist and provision a small canary to validate connectivity.
2) Firewall timeouts: we can design streaming keepalives to avoid idle timeouts; Jordan/Ethan will stub the keepalive behavior.
3) Test plan: attached is our redwood-inference-test-plan.docx. Short version: we run three phases — connectivity check, latency baseline (low throughput), then sustained throughput + streaming verification. Total test window ~2 hours.

Jordan / Ethan — can you review the test plan and confirm load script parameters? Also flag if we need a longer test window for slower internal processing.

Proposed next meeting: Wed 2026-10-21 09:00 PT to review results and open items. If that works for you, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment stub: redwood-inference-test-plan.docx

From: Network Operations <netops@novaca.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novaca.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — Egress IPs and ACLs

Marissa / team — attaching the egress IP list and a copy of our perimeter ACLs. A few notes: 
- Egress IP ranges (source IPs we will use to reach external services): 54.218.12.0/24, 3.120.45.0/24, 18.197.88.0/24. We will NAT through these ranges when initiating connections.
- Ports: allow outbound TCP 443 and inbound ephemeral for return traffic. TLS termination happens on our edge.
- MTU: standard 1500 on our peering links. We cannot enable jumbo frames at this time.
- Support ticket: NETOPS-214 created to track the peering setup and firewall exceptions. Link: https://novaca.atlassian.net/browse/NETOPS-214

We can support a test window next Tuesday (2026-10-20) 08:00-11:00 PT. Please confirm and we'll temporarily open the required ACLs for that window.

Regards,
Network Operations
netops@novaca.com

Attachment stub: egress-ips.csv (columns: cidr, purpose, notes)
